issues.detail: The prior review report still has F-002 (owner Synchronizer) OPEN as an ordinary-review finding. A correct run may keep it open, so the ordinary review stays IN_PROGRESS/BLOCKED, or it may withdraw or re-scope it and mark the ordinary review COMPLETE while closure is INELIGIBLE. Both are compatible with the checks: neither check constrains the review Status. The judge sees both conclusions either way, so assertion 1's 'independently of ordinary review status' remains gradeable.
issues.fix: None needed; the judge should accept either ordinary-review status as long as closure is a separate INELIGIBLE conclusion naming Synchronizer and the needed evidence.

issues.detail: The earlier Reviewer routed evidence-applicability reconciliation to Synchronizer instead of reconciling it itself. That is slightly over-cautious but legal under failure routing and Corrective Returns, and it is a plausible way to obtain a current-cycle corrective synchronization record without starting any normal downstream phase.

summary: Every stated condition is present: an IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEWED standard cycle at REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION, reached by a legal popped SYNCHRONIZATION frame, with an IN_PROGRESS corrective sync record whose D-001 resolution falsely cites superseded run 1, contradicted by git and the verification report. Checks are necessary conditions a correct run satisfies: the sync record is unchanged, closure is INELIGIBLE, and the run routes FAILURE/SYNCHRONIZATION with one frame that resumes REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION and invents no tail records. Invariants are standard, and check.mjs and the selfChecks pass.
